messages:
maya: Heads-up — running a bring-up eval for quantized-ggml-7B and seeing nondeterministic samples when the batch contains padded sequences. Repro steps below, happens ~1 in 6 runs.

maya: Quick log snippet: 
```
batch sizes: [4]
seq_lens: [512, 512, 128, 128]
padding_token: 50256
sampling: top_p=0.92, temp=0.85
seed: 12345 (set per-run)
worker: gpu-2 (cuda-12.1)
output[0] != output[2] on same inputs across runs
```

maya: Note — if I reorder the batch so short sequences are first, flakiness moves with them. Feels like a buffer/rng handoff at the padding boundary.

sam: ugh. do you have a minimal script or harness config? sounds like RNG stream isn't tied to sample idx.

maya: pasted the harness loop: 
```
for batch in dataloader:
  tokens = pad(batch)
  runner.request(tokens, params)
  // runner uses a worker pool and rounds-robin assigns strips
```

maya: CI shows this as a flaky eval: pipeline/evals:seed-sanity failing occasionally. Seems correlated with sampler=multistream + continuous batching.

jia: @maya thanks for repro. We hit something like this last month but it was top-k interleaving, not padding. Quick hypothesis: when we pack sequences, worker A handles tokens 0..N and worker B starts with KV cache re-use, but RNG state only reseeded per-worker not per-sample, so short sequences that get assigned to different workers get different RNG offsets between runs.

jia: Two actionable checks: 1) confirm runner assigns RNG streams per-sample (recommended) vs per-worker, 2) inspect pad masking logic — if masked positions still advance the sampler RNG (e.g., calling sample_step for pad tokens) then stream offsets diverge.

trevor: I can repro locally with cpu backend using smaller batch sizes. Seems deterministic if I force seed_per_sample = true in the harness. Can push a small patch to the eval runner to flip that flag for our CI and see if flakes go away.

maya: That'd be great. If it's seed-per-sample that's the fix we should probably adopt by default for evals (even if slightly slower) — correctness first.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Deployed rev c7f5a3 to staging 1759342175 (eng-ml-runner).

sam: quick test idea: add a unit test that creates 2 batches with identical multistream random draws but different pad orderings and assert outputs equal when seed_per_sample enabled. Also assert inequality when seed_per_sample disabled (to catch regressions intentionally).

jia: Also check quantized kernels: before we assume RNG issue — there was one quant path that used a shared workspace and had a stray pointer increment that only triggered on specific alignment (i.e., when padded sequences caused odd buffer sizing). The patch from Jan fixed pointer overflow but we may have a sibling bug.

maya: Agreed. Plan: trevor will push runner patch to enable seed_per_sample behind a feature-flag and add the unit tests. I'll instrument the harness to log worker assignment and RNG offset per-sample (minimal, stripped values) and run the full eval 100x.

trevor: Will open PR and add CI job: evals/sampler/regression-padding-100x. If results are green we'll flip feature-flag default for evals.

sam: please include a small reproducer script that anyone can run (single python file) — saves time during oncall.

maya: will do — attaching minimal script here in thread (inline): 
```
# repro.py (pseudo)
for i in range(20):
  batch = make_batch([512,512,128,128])
  out = runner.sample(batch, seed=12345)
  print(hash(out))
```

maya: thanks all — low-priority incident but high-impact for eval stability. cc @eng-sre if CI churn spikes. :pray:

jia: thanks. I'll also grep logs for any occurrences where `sample_step` is called with `is_padding=True` and see if we incorrectly advance RNG.

trevor: PR 982 incoming in ~1h.

sam: nice. when PR lands, I'll run the failing benchmark set 50x in staging.

maya: last note — noticed this only reproduces when top_p in (0.85..0.95). temp extremes (0.1 or 1.2) behave more stable either because sampling deterministic-ish or more entropy masks the drift. worth adding in test matrix.

jia: good catch. add param sweep to tests.

ops-bot: ci-bot: job evals/sampler/regression-padding-100x queued at 1759342250.

maya: thanks all, will follow up with results.
